rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud prayed that God show mercy to whoever gives charity and then prays, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: رحم الله امرأً تصدق ثم صلى ،   ثم يقرأ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reports that Ibn Umar checked after the Eid morning prayer whether the fitr charity had been given; if not, he ordered it given before going to the prayer ground.
rows.anchor: يا نافع أخرجت الصدقة ؟ فإن قلت : نعم ،   مضى إلى المصلى

rows.speaker: أبو العالية وابن سيرين
rows.claim: They take the passage to refer to giving zakat al-fitr and performing the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: قد أفلح من تزكى * وذكر اسم ربه فصلى } وهو قول أبي العالية وابن سيرين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed critic questions this interpretation because the sura is Meccan, when there was neither Eid nor fitr charity in Mecca.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه السورة مكية ،   ولم يكن بمكة عيد ولا زكاة فطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawi answers that revelation may precede the legal ruling, as with the Meccan verses about Muhammad being permitted in Mecca and the defeat of the enemy host, fulfilled later at the conquest and Badr.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون النزول سابقاً على الحكم كما قال : { وأنت حل بهذا البلد }

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says he did not know which host would be defeated until Badr, when he saw the Prophet recite the prediction while standing in his armor.
rows.anchor: كنت لا أدري أي جمع يهزم ،   فلما كان يوم بدر رأيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يثبت في الدرع

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation takes remembrance as the Eid takbirs and prayer as the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: قيل : الذكر : تكبيرات العيد ،   والصلاة : صلاة العيد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the prayer here to mean supplication.
rows.anchor: والصلاة : صلاة العيد ،   وقيل : الصلاة ها هنا الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sura has thirty verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الفجر مكية وآياتها ثلاثون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Abu Salih, identifies the oath as the break of dawn each day; Ikrima also holds this view.
rows.anchor: هو انفجار الصبح كل يوم وهو قول عكرمة

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya's report from Ibn Abbas interprets the dawn as the morning prayer.
rows.anchor: عنه : صلاة الصبح .   وقال قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies it as the dawn of the first day of Muharram, from which the year begins.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : هو فجر أول يوم من المحرم ،   تنفجر منه السنة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies it as the dawn of Dhu al-Hijja, since the ten nights are mentioned alongside it.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : فجر ذي الحجة لأنه قرن به الليالي العشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction means “and by Thamud,” carrying the oath preposition over to Thamud.
rows.anchor: أي : وبثمود ،   { الذين جابوا الصخر } قطعوا الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cut stone; صخرة is the singular form, and the people of Wadi al-Qura cut mountains into dwellings.
rows.anchor: جابوا الصخر } قطعوا الحجر ،   واحدتها : صخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley is Wadi al-Qura, where Thamud carved houses into the mountains.
rows.anchor: يعني : وادي القرى كانوا يقطعون الجبال فيجعلون فيها بيوتاً

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain the final yāʾ of al-wādī in both connected and paused reading, preserving the original form.
rows.anchor: وأثبت ابن كثير ويعقوب الياء في الوادي وصلا ووقفاً على الأصل

rows.speaker: ورش
rows.claim: Warsh retains the yāʾ in connected recitation only.
rows.anchor: وأثبتها ورش وصلاً

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation, matching the verse endings.
rows.anchor: والآخرون بحذفها في الحالين على وفق رؤوس الآي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh; they sinned and acted arrogantly on earth.
rows.anchor: يعني عاداً وثمود وفرعون ،   عملوا في الأرض بالمعاصي وتجبروا

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
rows.claim: The Hijaz and Basra readers retain the yāʾ in the connected forms أكرمني and أهانني.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة أكرمني وأهانني بإثبات الياء في الوصل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub also retain the yāʾ when pausing.
rows.anchor: ويقف ابن كثير ويعقوب بالياء أيضاً

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused forms.
rows.anchor: والآخرون يحذفونها وصلاً ووقفاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and poverty do not determine honor or humiliation: God grants and restricts provision by decree, including to disbelievers and believers respectively; true honor comes through obedience and disgrace through disobedience.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أن الإكرام والإهانة لا تدور على المال وسعة الرزق ،   ولكن الفقر والغنى بتقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke denies that abundant provision proves divine favor or that poverty proves divine contempt.
rows.anchor: فرد الله على من ظن أن سعة الرزق إكرام وأن الفقر إهانة ،   فقال : { كلا } لم أبتله بالغني لكرامته

rows.speaker: أهل البصرة
rows.claim: Basra reads the four verbs about honoring, urging, eating, and loving in the third person with yāʾ; the other readers use second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل لبصرة :  "  يكرمون ،   ويحضون ،   ويأكلون ،   ويحبون "  بالياء فيهن ،   وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke means that they do not treat the orphan well; another explanation is that they withhold the orphan's due.
rows.anchor: لا تحسنون إليه .   وقيل : لا تعطونه حقه .   قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيماً

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Qudama ibn Mazun was an orphan in Umayya ibn Khalaf's care, and Umayya denied him his right.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيماً في حجر أمية بن خلف وكان يدفعه عن حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not urge others to feed the poor.
rows.anchor: أي لا تأمرون بإطعامه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة
rows.claim: Abu Jafar and the Kufans read the verb with an open ḥāʾ and a following alif, meaning that people do not urge one another.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة : { تحاضون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها ،   أي لا يحض بعضكم بعضاً عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jamman means abundant: they love accumulating wealth and are passionately attached to it; the idiom جم الماء means water grew plentiful and gathered.
rows.anchor: يعني : تحبون جمع المال ويولعون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker wishes he had sent good deeds ahead for his afterlife, the life in which there is no death.
rows.anchor: أي قدمت الخير والعمل الصالح لحياتي في الآخرة ،   أي لآخرتي التي لا موت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul believes what God has said and is at rest concerning His promises.
rows.anchor: إلى ما وعد الله عز وجل المصدقة بما قال الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: For Mujahid, the tranquil soul is certain that God is its Lord and patiently remains firm in His command and obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { المطمئنة } التي أيقنت أن الله تعالى ربها وصبرت جاشاً لأمره وطاعته .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls it the believing soul, certain in faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : المؤمنة الموقنة ،   وقال عطية : الراضية بقضاء الله تعالى .

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya says it is content with God's decree.
rows.anchor: وقال عطية : الراضية بقضاء الله تعالى .   وقال الكلبي : الآمنة من عذاب الله .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it is safe from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الآمنة من عذاب الله .   وقيل : المطمئنة بذكر الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the soul is tranquil through remembrance of God, as in the verse about hearts finding rest through God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المطمئنة بذكر الله ،   بيانه : قوله { وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله }

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One group says the address is spoken at death: return to God, content with the reward and pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم : يقال لها ذلك عند الموت فيقال لها : { ارجعي إلى ربك } إلى الله

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes the soul at God's taking it as tranquil toward God, content with Him, and itself pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضي الله عنها .

rows.speaker: عبد الله ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar describes the believer's soul welcomed at death by angels, brought to God, and placed with believers in a fragrant, spacious grave; the disbeliever's soul is sent out amid stench and threatened with Hell and God's anger.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمر : إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله عز وجل ملكين ،   وأرسل إليه بتحفة من الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the return address is spoken as the soul leaves this world, while entry among God's servants and into His garden is said at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية } قال : هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group places the address at resurrection, when souls are ordered to return to their bodies; this is attributed to Ikrima, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنما يقال لها ذلك عند البعث .   { ارجعي إلى ربك } أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets return as return to God's reward: the soul is content with what God prepared, and God is pleased with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك راضيةً عن الله بما أعد لها ،   مرضيةً رضي الله عنها ربها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul believes what God has said and is at rest concerning His promises.
rows.anchor: إلى ما وعد الله عز وجل المصدقة بما قال الله

rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { المطمئنة } التي أيقنت أن الله تعالى ربها وصبرت جاشاً لأمره وطاعته .

rows.claim: Al-Hasan calls it the believing soul, certain in faith.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : المؤمنة الموقنة ،   وقال عطية : الراضية بقضاء الله تعالى .

rows.claim: Atiyya says it is content with God's decree.
rows.anchor: وقال عطية : الراضية بقضاء الله تعالى .   وقال الكلبي : الآمنة من عذاب الله .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says it is safe from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الآمنة من عذاب الله .   وقيل : المطمئنة بذكر الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the soul is tranquil through remembrance of God, as in the verse about hearts finding rest through God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المطمئنة بذكر الله ،   بيانه : قوله { وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله }

rows.claim: One group says the address is spoken at death: return to God, content with the reward and pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم : يقال لها ذلك عند الموت فيقال لها : { ارجعي إلى ربك } إلى الله

rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes the soul at God's taking it as tranquil toward God, content with Him, and itself pleasing to Him.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا أراد الله قبضها اطمأنت إلى الله ورضيت عن الله ورضي الله عنها .

rows.anchor: قال عبد الله ابن عمر : إذا توفي العبد المؤمن أرسل الله عز وجل ملكين ،   وأرسل إليه بتحفة من الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the return address is spoken as the soul leaves this world, while entry among God's servants and into His garden is said at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية } قال : هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another group places the address at resurrection, when souls are ordered to return to their bodies; this is attributed to Ikrima, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنما يقال لها ذلك عند البعث .   { ارجعي إلى ربك } أي إلى صاحبك وجسدك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets return as return to God's reward: the soul is content with what God prepared, and God is pleased with it.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : معناه : ارجعي إلى ثواب ربك راضيةً عن الله بما أعد لها ،   مرضيةً رضي الله عنها ربها .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enter among My servants means enter Paradise together with God's servants; another explanation is to join His righteous, obedient, chosen servants, as in the prayer of Solomon.
rows.anchor: يعني مع عبادي في جنتي .   وقيل : في جملة عبادي الصالحين المطيعين المصطفين

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
rows.claim: An inward reading addresses the soul attached to worldly life: return to God by leaving it, since return to God means following the path of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة : يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها ،   والرجوع إلى الله هو سلوك سبيل الآخرة .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that at Ibn Abbas's funeral in Taif a strange bird entered his bier and was not seen leaving; these verses were recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : مات ابن عباس بالطائف فشهدت جنازته ،   فجاء طائر لم ير على صورة خلقه فدخل نعشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahlaqt means spent; lubadan means abundant wealth piled up, spent in hostility toward Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني أنفقت ،   { مالاً لبداً } أي : كثيراً بعضه على بعض ،   من التلبيد ،   في عداوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar reads lubad with a doubled bāʾ, treating it as the plural of labid, like rākʿ and rukkaʿ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر { لبد } بتشديد الباء على جمع لابد ،   مثل راكع وركع

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: The other readers use a light bāʾ, either as the plural of libda or as a singular form like Qutham and Hutam.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالتخفيف على جمع لبدة ،   وقيل على الواحد مثل قثم وحطم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
rows.claim: They explain the question as asking whether he thinks God did not see him or will not question where he acquired and spent his wealth.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة : أيظن أن الله لم يره ،   ولا يسأله عن ماله من أين اكتسبه ،   وأين أنفقه ؟

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the man falsely boasts of spending more than he actually did, imagining God did not see and know the amount.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : إنه كان كاذباً في قوله أنفقت كذا وكذا ،   ولم يكن أنفق جميع ما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds the person of His favors so that he will reflect; He gave him eyes, a tongue, and lips.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكره نعمه ليعتبر فقال :{ ألم نجعل له عينين ولساناً وشفتين }

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God's successive favors confront and remind a person so that he will give thanks.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : نعم الله متظاهرة يقررك بها كيما تشكر

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith reports God saying that He gave a person ways to restrain forbidden speech, sight, and sexual desire by closing the lips, eyes, and other bodily means.
rows.anchor: في الحديث : " أن الله عز وجل يقول : ابن آدم إن نازعك لسانك فيما حرمت عليك فقد أعنتك عليه بطبقتين فأطبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud denied the truth because of their tyranny and aggression; their transgression drove them to denial.
rows.anchor: بطغيانها وعدوانها ،   أي الطغيان حملهم على التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is Salih, who warns the people not to hamstring God's she-camel and not to interfere with its allotted drink from the water.
rows.anchor: { فقال لهم رسول الله } صالح { ناقة الله } أي احذروا عقر ناقة الله .

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the accusative naqat Allah implies an omitted command: leave God's she-camel alone.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : منصوب على معنى : ذروا ناقة الله ،   { وسقياها } شربها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: By the same ellipsis, leave her drink alone and do not approach the water on her drinking day.
rows.anchor: أي : ذروا ناقة الله وذروا شربها من الماء ،   فلا تعرضوا للماء يوم شربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied Salih and hamstrung the she-camel.
rows.anchor: فكذبوه } يعني صالحاً ،   { فعقروها } يعني الناقة

rows.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ata and Muqatil explain damdama as God destroying and annihilating them.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء ومقاتل : فدمر عليهم ربهم فأهلكهم

rows.speaker: المدرج
rows.claim: Al-Mudarrij defines damdama as annihilation that leaves nothing.
rows.anchor: قال المدرج : الدمدمة الهلاك باستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sin was denying the Messenger and hamstringing the she-camel.
rows.anchor: بذنبهم } بتكذيبهم الرسول وعقرهم الناقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment engulfed all of them, and none escaped.
rows.anchor: فسواها } الدمدمة عليهم جميعاً ،   وعمهم بها فلم يفلت منهم أحد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says God leveled the people by punishing young and old alike, making them equal.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : سوى الأمة وأنزل العذاب بصغيرها وكبيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan sura has twenty-one verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الليل مكية وآياتها إحدى وعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night covers the day with darkness and removes its light.
rows.anchor: أي يغشى النهار بظلمة فيذهب بضوئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the answer to the oath: deeds differ, as some strive to free themselves and others to ruin themselves.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم قوله :{ إن سعيكم لشتىً } إن أعمالكم لمختلفة

rows.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Malik al-Ashari reports the Prophet saying that everyone starts the day selling himself, either freeing or destroying himself.
rows.anchor: روى أبو مالك الأشعري قال : "  قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : كل الناس يغدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver spends his wealth in God's cause and fears his Lord.
rows.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } ماله في سبيل الله ،   { واتقى } ربه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن والضحاك
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman and al-Dahhak explain al-husna as the testimony that there is no god but God; this is also Atiyya's report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن والضحاك : وصدق بلا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says al-husna means Paradise, supported by the verse promising al-husna to those who do good.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بالجنة ،   دليله : قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes al-husna as God's replacement or recompense, trusted to be provided; this is Ikrima's report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقيل { صدق بالحسنى } : أي بالخلف ،   أي أيقن أن الله تعالى سيخلفه

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi interpret it as believing God's promise, which God will fulfill.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي : بموعود الله عز وجل الذي وعده أن يفي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will prepare the giver in this world for the easy course: acting in ways that please God.
rows.anchor: فسنهيئه في الدنيا ،   { لليسرى } أي للخلة اليسرى ،   وهي العمل بما يرضاه الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds charitable spending, considers himself independent of God's reward, and does not seek it.
rows.anchor: { وأما من بخل } بالنفقة في الخير ،   { واستغنى } عن ثواب الله فلم يرغب فيه

none: Verse text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the denier for evil, letting him perform what displeases God until he deserves the Fire.
rows.anchor: سنهيئه للشر بأن نجريه على يديه حتى يعمل بما لا يرضي الله ،   فيستوجب به النار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God makes it difficult for the person to do good.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : نعسر عليه أن يأتي خيراً

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports the Prophet saying every soul's destination is recorded, but people must still act: each is facilitated for the deeds of the blessed or wretched, and the Prophet recited these verses.
rows.anchor: وروينا عن علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " ما من نفس منفوسة إلا كتب الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
rows.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wealth, which he withheld, will not benefit him when he falls.
rows.anchor: وما يغني عنه ماله }الذي بخل به ،   { إذا تردى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the fall as death.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : إذا مات

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Qatada and Abu Salih say it means falling into Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو صالح : هوى في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance here means clarification.
rows.anchor: عني البيان

rows.speaker: الزجاج وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Qatada say God undertakes to clarify guidance and misguidance; Qatada specifies the lawful and forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : علينا أن نبين طريق الهدى من طريق الضلال ،   وهو قول قتادة ،   قال : على الله بيان حلاله وحرامه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads it as God's undertaking of the way for whoever follows guidance, comparing the verse that says the straight path belongs to God.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : يعني من سلك الهدى فعلى الله سبيله ،   كقوله تعالى : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل }

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes both guidance and misguidance under God's power, as in the statement that good is in God's hand.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : إن علينا للهدى والإضلال كقوله : { بيدك الخير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns both the afterlife and this world; whoever seeks them from anyone other than their owner has taken the wrong path.
rows.anchor: فمن طلبهما من غير مالكهما فقد أخطأ الطريق

none: Verse text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched enters that Fire.
rows.anchor: لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most wretched is the one who denied the Messenger and turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: الذي كذب } الرسول ،   { وتولى } عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched denotes the miserable person, and the most God-fearing denotes the pious person.
rows.anchor: يريد بالأشقى الشقي ،   وبالأتقى التقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives his wealth seeking purity with God, without ostentation or desire for reputation; all identify him as Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: يتزكى } يطلب أن يكون عند الله زاكياً لا رياء ولا سمعة ،   يعني أبا بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed enslaved weak people; when his father suggested buying stronger allies, Abu Bakr answered that he sought protection for his own back, and the passage through the end of the sura was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الزبير : كان أبو بكر يبتاع الضعفة فيعتقهم ،   فقال أبوه : أي بني لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك ؟

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Bilal ibn Rabah, son of Hamama, was tortured by Umayya ibn Khalaf in Mecca's noonday heat, pinned beneath a boulder and told to renounce Muhammad; he kept saying Ahad, Ahad.
rows.anchor: وذكر محمد بن إسحاق قال : كان بلال لبعض بني جمع وهو بلال بن رباح واسم أمه حمامة

rows.speaker: هشام بن عروة عن أبيه
rows.claim: Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, reports Abu Bakr challenging Umayya over Bilal's torture, exchanging a strong enslaved man for Bilal, and freeing him.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق ،   عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال : مر به أبو بكر يوماً وهم يصنعون به ذلك

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq lists six other people Abu Bakr freed before the migration: Amir ibn Fuhayra, Umm Umays, Zahra, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, and a girl of Banu al-Muammal.
rows.anchor: ثم أعتق معه على الإسلام قبل أن يهاجر ست رقاب ،   بلال سابعهم وهم : عامر بن فهيرة

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq adds that Quraysh blamed the idols for Zahra's impaired sight, but she denied their power and her sight returned; Abu Bakr bought al-Nahdiyya and her daughter despite their mistress's refusal, and freed a tortured Banu al-Muammal girl.
rows.anchor: فأصيب بصرها وأعتقها ،   فقالت قريش : ما أذهب بصرها إلا اللات والعزى فقالت : كذبوا وبيت الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalls the Prophet's condition before revelation and reminds him of His favors.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبره الله عز وجل عن حالته التي كان عليها قبل الوحي ،   وذكر نعمه فقال جل ذكره :

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking about gifts given to other men; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him. Other transmitters add that God expanded his breast and removed his burden.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad was a poor child, his parents died without leaving property or shelter; God gave him refuge with his uncle Abu Talib, who raised and provided for him.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية : ألم يجدك يتيماً صغيراً فقيراً حين مات أبواك ولم يخلفا لك مالاً ولا مأوىً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was astray from the state he now has, and God guided him to monotheism and prophethood.
rows.anchor: يعني ضالاً عما أنت عليه فهداك للتوحيد والنبوة

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وابن كيسان
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Kaysan say he was unaware of prophetic signs and the law before revelation, and God guided him to them.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن والضحاك وابن كيسان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he was lost in Mecca's valleys and God guided him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: وقال : ضالاً في شعاب مكة فهداك إلى جدك عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as a small child the Prophet became lost in Mecca's valleys; Abu Jahl found him turning away from his flock and returned him to Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: روى أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس  "  أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صبي صغير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib recounts that during a night journey with Abu Talib's caravan, the Devil led Muhammad's camel off course; Gabriel blew the Devil to Abyssinia and returned Muhammad to the caravan.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب : خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في قافلة مسيرة غلام خديجة فبينما هو راكب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view says God found him not knowing himself or his identity, then made him know himself and his condition.
rows.anchor: وقيل : وجدك ضالاً ضال نفسك لا تدري من أنت ،   فعرفك نفسك وحالك .
